exposure: maternal characteristics (age, parity, assisted reproductive technology use)
reasons for ICU admission (postpartum hemorrhage, hypertensive disorders of pregnancy)
cohort: The study included pregnant or postpartum women admitted to the intensive care unit of a Portuguese tertiary hospital over a 15-year period.
finding: The study found that obstetric ICU admissions primarily occurred in the early postpartum period after cesarean section, with postpartum hemorrhage and hypertensive disorders being the most frequent causes, resulting in a 1.3% maternal mortality rate and 46.4% neonatal ICU admissions.
mod_finding: Most obstetric ICU admissions (74%) occurred after a cesarean section, and severe postpartum hemorrhage, a common reason for admission, prompted a reassessment of delivery practices.
